strings.name: George Miller
strings.summary: Born in Queensland, Miller trained in medicine and worked in hospitals before building a filmmaking partnership with Byron Kennedy. The low-budget Mad Max launched a post-apocalyptic action series whose movement and visual storytelling influenced international cinema. He also directed Lorenzo’s Oil and Happy Feet and co-wrote and produced Babe. Furiosa arrived in 2024, continuing a career spanning action, animation and other narrative forms.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through the Mad Max series and animation, he advances visual storytelling in action films and the international reach of Australian cinema.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied medicine at the University of New South Wales and worked in hospitals while developing filmmaking interests.
strings.highlights.h1.title: The Mad Max series
strings.highlights.h1.text: From the 1979 debut to Fury Road and Furiosa, developed traditions in action, staging and visual storytelling.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Work across genres
strings.highlights.h2.text: Moved from medical drama to family films and animation; Happy Feet won the animated-feature Oscar.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Released Furiosa
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Mad Max prequel premiered at Cannes, expanding its world and characters.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released Three Thousand Years of Longing
strings.timeline.t2.text: The fantasy about storytelling screened out of competition at Cannes.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Released Fury Road
strings.timeline.t3.text: The series returned; the film won six Oscars the next year and earned Miller a directing nomination.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Happy Feet won an Oscar
strings.timeline.t4.text: His 2006 animated film received Best Animated Feature.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-wrote and produced Babe
strings.timeline.t5.text: Contributed writing and production; Chris Noonan directed the film.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Directed Lorenzo’s Oil
strings.timeline.t6.text: A medical and ethical drama based on a family’s search for treatment for a rare disease.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Directed The Witches of Eastwick
strings.timeline.t7.text: Expanded into Hollywood production with supernatural comedy.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Released first Mad Max
strings.timeline.t8.text: The low-budget film made with Byron Kennedy began a long-running franchise.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Made early short film
strings.timeline.t9.text: Collaborated with Kennedy on Violence in the Cinema, Part 1 while moving from medicine toward film.
